text_fidelity_a:
Logo Board Game For what it is, a trivia game just based on popular brands, this is probably as good as it gets.

The gameplay is simple, and they've devised a way to play with only using cards and the board, so no die required. The board is a path made up of 4 colors that the instructions say are in 'random' order. And even though the random order would never pass any randomness tests, it makes for game play that moves along.

The cards are the best part. Each card is usually dedicated to a different brand, so you could just thumb through the cards and pick your favorite brands by the pictures on the faces of the cards.

And, you'll probably wonder, since playing this is really similar to watching a couple hours of commercials, "Shouldn't they be paying me to play this game?"

Pros:
+Tons of trivia about tons of different companies
+You can play without dice, so this will last a lot longer than most board games
+Both easy and hard trivia questions, so people don't feel too stupid
+Even if you are really bad at trivia, this game will only take about an hour to play (15 minutes if you're awesome)

Cons:
-All the standard cons that go along with a trivia game. It makes the smart people feel smarter, and the dumb people feel dumber. I'm pretty dumb at trivia, so it was nice to play a trivia game and only feel mildly dumb.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Update:
I got a blue top this time to head-swap with Barbie Paleontologist. I really loved the pretty dimples of Blue Top Barbie. I hope to get another one soon. This one could even stand in flat shoes. Her ankles were just right. Some of the other Barbie Made to Move dolls had tricky little ankles with a mind all their own.
Also the peg inside their heads are slightly different, so the neck on one doll looks shorter now.
I just got Barbie Made to Move today. I read many reviews about Barbie Made to Move vs. Style Barbie. I just had to try her out. Most people who have the 2 dolls say Made to Move Barbie is a much better poser. This is very true.
I liked the rooted lashes and 2-toned hair on Style Barbie the best, so I can't say Style Barbie is a loser. Style also has the bending ankle and can wear both flats and heels. Made to move Barbie has choppy hair. I like it just the same, because my real hair is not all the same length. I thought it looked nice.
Made to Move Barbie can bend her knees all the way back and sit down on her knees. She can bend at the breast/ rib cage, but not at the waist. Style Barbie cannot do any of this.
Style Barbie can only bend her knees to sit down in a chair.
Made to Move Barbie can spread her legs out like in yoga or exercise class. Style Barbie can spread her legs very little in comparison.
Made to Move Barbie has much sturdier looking joints except in the ankles, they are almost the same. One thing I did notice was one of her ankles turns inward like she needs her electrolytes. I thought it was the shoes but I traded their shoes around and noticed the shoes were okay. I still like the natural looking poses for this doll. She is a much better choice for those who love doll dioramas and modelling clothes.

As soon as I got her out, I noticed one small dot on her foot and face both barely noticeable. To me personally, this is not a problem, but I thought I should mention it. The price was well worth it for this doll. The clothes are nice enough and stretchy so I can go ahead and pose her. I had a couple of pairs of Barbie shoes to try on her. She came barefooted. I was thrilled to find that her jointed ankle makes it possible for her to wear high heels and flat shoes made for Barbie. I have both branded and unbranded Barbie shoes that fit her. I was almost about to sell some of the shoes when I got her, but she is a keeper and loves shoes. The usual Barbie seams are kind of rough in places but that is okay, considering what I paid for her ($11.04). I consider this to be a really great buy.

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark and the DJI Tello, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for 35 dollars. Compared to other drones, I would say that there are certain improvements that could be made but those drones are much, much more expensive.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is quite small, which is nice because it lends itself to indoor flight and easy travel. It is about 4.5 inches by 4.5 inches for a length and width, and the diagonal rotor distance is about 5 inches, while to entire copter stands at about 1.25 inches. This, as I said, is nice for indoor flight and you don't have to worry too much about hitting someone. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards proved themselves quite useful, as I bumped it into walls several times, and the guards did their job. The copter simply bounced off the wall and continued flying. Additionally, when I was testing it, the drone died while flying. I knew this was coming, as I could feel the responsiveness beginning to slow and the flip function would no longer work. The drone fell from about 12 feet in the air onto the blacktop. I didn't notice and dings, dents, or scar=tches, and once it was charged, it flew fine.

Quiet - The drone has a shrill high pitched sound as it flies. It isn't too loud, and I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. Executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward of backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button a the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Cons:
Disproportionate flight to charge time ratio - According to the user manual, this charge time is about 70 minutes, while the flight time is around 5 minutes while hovering. I, however, found that it took about 35 minutes (charging for a wall outlet) for a full charge from dropping out of the sky dead. The flight time that I got was about 6 minutes, doing maneuvers, flips, climbing, falling, accelerating and decelerating. Still, I think this could be improved, and, as there are no removable batteries you can plug in once another is dead, I make using the drone for more than 10 minutes hard.
Poor wind resistance - This thing blows outside with the slightest breeze. Inside, the flight trim is hard to adjust, and outside, it is not worth it. I found myself constantly adjusting to compensate for any wind.
Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as find things within the manual. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
Joysticks don't articulate much - This is actually somewhat annoying. there isn't much height to the sticks, and they don't move around much, making any more precise movements difficult. Additionally, the other buttons on the controller are somewhat difficult to press.

I liked this drone, especially for the price. This would be great for any kid, or even as a starting copter for someone who wants to see if they are interested in them. I like the size, durability, and flip function, but the battery life and wind resistance are something to consider.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls

Lots of nostalgia, lots of little visual cues to make it fun. But whoever designed the cut out portion did an awful job.

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog Sometimes when I get a box of Bloks, I chuck the instructions, dump them in with the rest of my collection, and make something cool with some of my favorite new pieces. I really liked the look of this one though, and I haven't followed the instructions for a while, so I actually built it to spec. I wasn't sure if there was any logic to all the separate and nested baggies, but half way through I concluded that the answer was "very little". I dumped them all in a dark colored jewelry display tray and things went much more smoothly. I definitely learned a few things about how some of the pieces can work together, and the end result came out looking nicer than most of the pre-built toys out there these days, but fully customizable. There are quite a lot of Bloks left over after completing the main instructions, and they've included some suggested modifications with build instructions, like the missile launcher in one of the pictures.

There were some minor flaws. The windshield doesn't attach very solidly. The two dudes are so burly and heavily armored that they don't fit inside gracefully. A few of the pieces shrunk just enough when they cooled that they ripple a bit differently than the things they are supposed to look smooth with. Lastly, while the instructions are very good, this set is mostly different shades of black and dark silver, which weren't adequately differentiated in the pictures which made locating the right parts in the heap difficult

The build process, with its sorting and instruction struck me as.something that would be a good project to do with my 3 year old son, since he is developing all the needed skills right now. Maybe instead of a puzzle, we'll build a warthog together on the next rainy day.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks HALO Dual Mode UNSC Warthog

Driven by Battat - Fire Truck - Toy Vehicle We have three Driven Trucks. The garbage truck, the dumpster, and this fire engine.
We rated the other two 5 stars. This one is 3.5 to 4 stars. Generously rounded up to 4 stars.

The company did a good job of designing a realistic looking fire truck. They may have overdone the features. The hose is our main complaint. The crank handle was difficult for an adult to turn. This problem appears to vary with each unit. For example, others complained about hard to turn cranks on the garbage trucks. Ours was very smooth on the garbage truck. The hose looks very fragile. We elected not to put water in the reservoir. Unfortunate, because it would have been a fun feature.

Other than the hose issue, it’s a nice item. The main ladder cranks up easily, and then a second, smaller crank handle take another section higher. That is a very nice feature that our grandsons enjoy. The doors open, the lights go on when the engine is started, and the horn beeps. It is not motorized and the engine starts, but the truck does not move unless pushed.

Durability?

In addition to questionable durability on the hose, rough play may damage the large ladder which is the best feature of the truck. To date, the Fire Engine has stood up well to a 2 and 4 year old.
text_fidelity_b: Driven by Battat - Fire Truck - Toy Vehicle

Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+ I have very mixed feelings about this game. First, it is REALLY FUN, and my kids and I were laughing really hard playing it. The drone taking off is really a lot of fun and cool to see, and even our little 3 year old who is too young to play was enamored by it and shrieking when it would lift off with little playing pieces inside! Really a lot of fun.
That being said, there are 3 caveats to be aware of:
1)I don't feel comfortable letting the kids play this alone. The drone comes crashing down sometimes and I want an adult or kid old enough to be able to catch it to avoid hurting anyone / furniture, or crashing so hard it cracks the plastic (a part of the drone siding already popped out, but I was able to push it back into place).

2) I feel like this game won't last very long. The pieces are VERY easily lost, as they end up being flung around the room as you play. Also, the drone lifting off bumps into the ceiling easily (thankfully we have cathedral ceilings in our living and had to move the game over to there, otherwise it would hit and come crashing down fast). It's only a matter of time before the plastic breaks or pieces get lost forever.

3) I dove to catch it on the way down after a particular round, and it hurt my finger. Nothing major, didn't hurt more than stubbing your toe on furniture or stepping on a lego- it has a safety to shut the propeller if it detects something in the way, but I was still surprised. I was fine, but one of my kids would have been crying if it happened to them.

My daughter actually suggested we try playing it outside next time, which might solve some of the issues- can't do damage to the house and everyone can duck for cover until it crashes into the grass. Wind might make it less fun though. HOWEVER- this was a TON OF FUN TO PLAY, so even with all those caveats, and even considering it might not last more than a few months in my household, I'd still consider it worth playing even for those few times. The look on their faces when the drone takes off is PRICELESS, and worth it even if you only get to play it once.
text_fidelity_b: Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+

Jurassic World Bite 'n Fight Tyrannosaurus Rex in Larger Size with Realistic Sculpting, Articulation and Dual-Button Activation for Tail Strike and Head Strikes, Ages 4 and Older Wow! Wow wow wow!

That's pretty much what you're going to hear when you present this gift to a small person. A bunch of wows, and then a bunch of roaring after you get it out of the package and they start playing with it. There are two buttons in the middle of the T Rex, one of which works the tail and the other of which works the head and snapping jaws. The buttons are a little hard to press effectively to make the action occur, so small T Rex fans might have a little more trouble activating things than one might like, but there's a next to it, which bigger guys will soon figure out.

I picked this up because I have a Jurassic world toys truck, which is supposed to hold the dinosaur in the back. There's like this included shell that comes up over the top and is supposed to have the dinosaur's head sticking up out of the shell, and I thought that this T Rex, being from the same line, would fit gracefully in the back of that truck. Nope, this thing is huge. Huge huge. Check the measurements before expecting this to dovetail with any other toys because T Rex is a big dude.

The size and the snapping jaws action really contributes to the awesome gift presentation this makes. Does it have a lot of long-term play potential? I'm not really sure that it does, frankly. I think in our house, once I get tired of tripping over it, I'm going to relegate it to being a backyard toy and just allow it to slowly stop working. However, right now the kids are having a blast creating scenes for T Rex to come in and stomp. He is particularly good it crashing through block towers.

text_fidelity_a:
Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists. This kit was made to help families like ours. I am a stay at home mom to four kids (11yo and younger). Prior, I was an artist and earned a Special Ed and a Rehabilitation degree. My background has been useful because we ended up a household full of ADHD, severe anxiety, learning and speech disabilities, plus more. We have been using this set for three weeks now and it has proven invaluable. It truly was an excellent find.

We do not own the original set (with the Dove on the box), but I suspect this new version is probably an upgraded improvement of the first box set. It looks very similar, except now there appears have some new (maybe better) ideas and slightly more guidance in this new version. I don't mean to imply this set is a duplicate of the first set, nor am I trying to discourage you from buying both. I simply don't know. I came to the conclusion that these were similar after reading the reviews for the first one. Had I been given the option to chose between the two sets, I would have chosen to start with the newer set I am reviewing here today. Simply because of the changes that were made.

ABOUT THE PRODUCT:

- Most of the cards appear to have between 200 to 300 words. Each activity lasts about 5 minutes per card, give or take. Of course each could be longer or shorter because you get decide how much time you want to spend.

- This newer set has a total of 24 meditation activity cards. 18 of the 24 are guided scenarios. The 18 cards are "story like, short guided imaginary meditation with different scenes that people can imagine themselves taking a part of.” Meaning they ask you to concentrate and imagine yourself in a particular story line (like "walking through the woods" or "stargazing on a warm summer night", for example).
- 6 of those 18 cards mentioned above focus on our senses (touch, taste, etc).
- In addition to the above 18, there are 6 more "positive affirmation" cards. These affirmations address different times of day (morning or bedtime) -or- feelings (anger, stress, etc).

OTHER COMPARISON NOTES:
- From what I can tell, the original set only appears to have 23 guided imaginary "walk through the woods" type scenarios. It does not specifically explore common human experiences that center around feeling or our body.
- The Legend Card is unique to this set. The Legend is more of a guide chart that will help you quickly find the most useful card, depending on the your feelings/needs at the moment­.
- Both sets have the same breathing exercise card.

MY POSITIVES:

- This set is excellent quality. The cards are very nice and are made of a thick paperboard. They are technically laminated, though it wouldn't consider it a plastic waterproof type of covering. It feels more like a wax coating that is water resistant. But it is a sturdy material.
-This truly is an activity for all ages. Kids 6 and younger will probably need guidance. Around 6 or 7, this could probably be an independent activity for most kids. But this mediation set is NOT just for kids. I think pre-teens, teens, and even adults can still benefit from these cards. I wish I made more time to use them myself, tbh.
- These have been excellent in helping everyone in our house decompress and cope with our daily stressors.
- I think this encourages and even teaches how to use our imaginations better (an essential skill!!!).
- It has increases our awareness of self worth. And in a sense, these also teach us to take responsibility for some of our thoughts and feelings too. These activities seem to encourage future motivation and action too.
-This kit is secular and inclusive. Meaning it is not religions in any way. And Many people are represented in the images. The language the cards use, and the activities are age and gender neutral. The suggested scenarios are something anyone can envision.
- And the art is beautiful.

THE NEGATIVES:
- The box is terrible. It's too small. It's impossible to find the one card the Ledged Guide tells you to grab without taking out the entire stack. And it's a pain putting the cards away. I'm going to have to come up with a better storage system.
- There are spelling mistakes, improper punctuation, and unnecessary capitalization. If it had been here or there, I wouldn't have said anything. Nor am I in a position to judge. But it's really bad and does not feel educational.
- The price feels a bit steep initially. However, I think if you make it a goal to give this set a real try and use it for a little while, I think you'll see the $30 price tag actually feels like a good deal.

Overall, I definitely recommend trying this. It is unique and I wish I had know about the original set years ago. But I think this newer set was an even better find. We couldn't be happier. Thank you for reading this ridiculously long review and I hope it helped make your decision easier.
text_fidelity_b: Imagine Meditation Kit for Kids - Award-Winning Mindfulness kit of XL Cards with Calming Guided Meditations for Empowerment, Focus and Relaxation. Great for Parents, Teachers and Therapists.

My biggest problem is that the entire thing is made out of cardboard, and it won't last long enough for your child to actually practice with. Ours was in the trash after two days of very light use. As another reviewer mentioned, mine shipped with batteries, but those were dead.

As an idea, this is excellent. As a kit, you can pass.

text_fidelity_a:
Pass the Stache Board Game This is definitely not a cerebral or strategizing game. It is pure reaction, action, and laughter. We played a number of rounds as a way to break the ice between to families of children who had not met yet, and it was perfect. The rules are as simple as you can get, flip a card up, if it matches the color or shape of your mustache, hit it with your suction cupped mustache and claim the card. It you suction cup up one that doesn't match, you pay a two card penalty and he who ends with the most cards wins. Ok there are a couple more rules, but that is the gyst. There are also an all smash card and a none smash cards. But seriously, that is the rules right there.

The mustaches themselves are great. They are a blast in themselves as our kids giggled continually at the look of the mustaches touch to everyone's upper lip. They are made strong with decent suction cups below them. It is fairly easy to strike a card and pull it up with the suction cup. And the cards are well made to take the abuse.

As for game play, the rounds are short and exciting. Some feelings got hurt, but for the most part it was an uproarious game which put smiles on everyone's face. Scoring is easy...just count up the cards you won. Personally, I don't think this will be a classic game, but it willl be pulled out in our house many times.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

Elmer’s Slime Kit Slime Supplies Include Elmer’s Metallic Glue, Elmer’s Magical Liquid Slime Activator, 4 Piece Kit As a family, we did this together and it was fun to do but, the results were inconsistent despite the measurements being done by the same person.

The set up and instructions are easy to follow but, I would definitely recommend an adult be involved with the process. The two batches we made we done per the instructions and it seems like a day later, they are different and have different consistencies. The first batch came out perfect. There is a lot of stirring and kneading that has to be done to get all of the clumps out for a smoother slime. The slime came out doughy and fun. The second batch, done at the same time, feels more wet and sticky than the first despite having mixed and kneaded more than the first batch. The color and glitter add ins are fun but aren’t as eye catching as I thought they’d be.

The thing I was absolutely disappointed in was that there wasn’t a container to put the slime in once the fun was over. We ended up putting them in sandwich bags until I can grab something from the store to hold them in. Overall, fun was had but, turned out a little frustrating that the results were so clearly different from one another.

Overall, I would still recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games Ok, so every 4th of July my rather decent sized family (~30 people) gets together and has a great time. A few of us in the younger age range (<30) love to play board games and stuff like that. We had played the same games for several years and I was getting board with the same stuff. I was looking for a new challenge!

I searched for weeks, looking for a game that I thought would suffice, and I kept coming back to cosmic encounters. I finally decided to buy it. When it came in the mail I ripped everything open and started discovering the game. I was so excited and hopeful. It looked pretty complicated, ever after watching How-To's online.

I tried to get a couple of my friends to play it, but after watching me setup the game (still barely having a clue how to play) they gave up and wanted to play 3's (a simple card game).

So there my expensive new game sat for weeks... months... a year! I finally got one of my cousins to play it with me, but we had to switch off playing a third person. We hardly had a clue how to play, but it sparked his interest.

The few times we got together after that, we just didn't get the time to play the game but his interest stayed.

Finally, a friend of mine and I went up to my cabin, and my cousin happened to be there.

I had brought the game, so we decided to finally play it the with the right number of players! After each of us read through the manual, we started playing. There was a fair amount of confusion with the rules, and how the game actually played out, but we managed to finish the game. We then played another, and another after that. The game was a blast! We discovered a new rule or something we hadn't been doing right practically every game. We actually played 3 or 4 whole games before we learned we were supposed to be able to get 2 encounters per turn!

Every game we played we got more and more accustomed to the game, and we enjoyed it a little more. I now cant wait to play it again, and I am getting more people involved with it. I am planning on buying the expansions as well!

Long story short, it is a somewhat difficult game to learn, but once you do it is a blast! Each game took about 30 minutes to an hour with three people.

I definitely recommend it if your looking for a good board game!
text_fidelity_b: Cosmic Encounter 42nd Anniversary Edition Board Game - Classic Strategy Game of Intergalactic Conquest for Kids and Adults, Ages 14+, 3-5 Players, 1-2 Hour Playtime, Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls I absolutely love dolls of all types and own hundreds of them. They range from inexpensive off-brand play dolls, legitimate BJDs, to high-end handmade artist dolls. This is likely the worst designed doll I have ever handled.

This doll has a very cute face and poses well. However, the deal-breaker is that she has No Neck! Her head sits right on her shoulders. This is very distracting because it makes it hard to look at her. I would be able to overlook so many of the other negative aspects to this doll if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. This is very disappointing. It's such a pity as she has a very pretty face.

This is not a BJD (ball-jointed doll). This doll shares a similar aesthetic to some BJDs, but she does not have even a single ball joint. She has hinge and swivel joints only. The doll is made from at least three different types of plastic. One maybe ABS plastic, but there are no silicone components to this doll.

Her hair is pretty rooted plugs. The description led me to believe it may be a wig, but no. The plugs are evenly spaced and I do not see any bald spots. The hair fibers are soft. The eyelashes are glued strips and the eyes are inset acrylics. She has very pretty face that is painted symmetrically. The joints were very, very stiff and difficult to loosen with force. Once loosened, she does pose decently and can touch her face. She has a full outfit that is made with flawed fabric. Several threads are missing in the weave of the fabric of the skirt. The flawed fabric is very noticeable. The outfit has a shirt, vest, skirt, bloomers, knee socks and a hat. It would be a very cute outfit if the stitching was a little more straight and the fabric was not deeply flawed fabric. The material is incredibly low quality. Her shoes are light purple canvas, do not match the outfit, but are fair quality and fit her flat feet snugly.

A packet of 'accessories' are included and is confusing. They are thin plastic, various shades of pink and not to scale with the doll. The comb and 4 little hair elastics may be useful to play with the doll but otherwise they would likely not be much fun for playing with the doll and I feel would be better left out of the package. Some heeled shoes were also included in the packet and although I could put them on the doll, the straps were useless and they looked odd as she has flat feet. Little fingers would likely become frustrated trying to fasten the straps.

I looked into the UCanaan brand after ordering this doll. I was disappointed to learn that the company uses re-casted parts from legitimate BJD makers without permission. This is very sad/bad news. I would have expected better from a US retail site and find it deeply disappointing. I do not know that any pieces are made from the re-casted parts from other companies for this particular doll, but it's a serious negative point that should be noted. I cannot say with confidence this is not a re-casted doll. I would not be surprised to learn that it is.

I cannot recommend this doll. The primary reasons being she has no neck, is not as described and the company does shady business practices. This makes me very uneasy as it sets up customers for some serious disappointment. If you are looking for a budget-friendly legitimate BJD, there are other companies that make very nice lower-cost dolls. It takes a minimum amount of looking off the site to find them. If you are looking for a nice doll for display, or posing and play, please note this one has no neck and uses poor quality materials. Your money would be better spent elsewhere. I do not find this to be a good value in the least. She would be enjoyable for display if she had a neck like the doll in the description photos. I hope that this can be remedied in the future. I find this doll very disappointing and it's such a pity as she would otherwise be very cute with an alternative outfit.

I do hope you have found my honest review helpful. If you do, please click the Helpful button below. Thank you for reading my review.
text_fidelity_b: UCanaan BJD Dolls 1/4 SD Doll 18 Inch 18 Ball Jointed Doll DIY Toys with Full Set Clothes Shoes Wig Makeup, Best Gift for Girls

32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories Pros: The kids love the kitchen playset, so much so that my 4.5-year-old niece preferred it to playing her favorite computer game for a full week and the 2-year-old couldn't be tempted away even by birthday cake. It's still the first toy she heads for when she visits. One kid can play on each side, so they can play at the same time. They didn't seem bothered that things didn't work quite right. I also like that they have whole food cooking ingredients (fruit, veggies, meat, eggs) rather than a bunch of finished foods or deserts.

Cons: The kitchen is basically held together by the parts having been firmly pressed into place. Thus, even lifting it by the roof can cause parts to come off. We've moved the kitchen around several times with no problem as long as you use the handles on the purple side panels. The oven and cupboard doors were initially hard to open, but luckily use has loosened this up some. The sink faucet pulls out during play, one of the BBQ-stick holders comes off very easily (when removing the stick to put food on or off), and some of the stickers don't want to stay on. Replacing the batteries is going to be a pain as they're on the underside of the cooking surface. The plastic food is a soft plastic, so the egg got crushed when stepped on. And cooking sure is noisy! I wish there was a way to lower the volume. So the adults feel like this isn't as good a product as it could be (3 stars) but the kids give it 5 stars.

ORIGINAL: This kitchen and grill playset is the perfect height for my two-year-old niece to play with. She likes to pretend like she is cooking, so she enjoys playing with the set. There is some assembly required, and the instructions are simply line drawings. Keep the box since looking at the two sides in the pictures is of more help in assembly than the instructions. Keep in mind that you will not fully tighten the joints until done with the first couple steps. The barbecue sign is a thin sheet of cardboard, so I assume that the thicker board is supposed to be put in the slot along with it. I don't know why they didn't just print the sign on the thicker board or even just past it on. As it is, you're trying to fit two separate sheets into a slot seemingly meant only for the thicker one. I had someone try to help me get it into the slot, but it was too tight to get in very far. I ended up cutting off some of the top just to make it fit (though it turns out I didn't need to do this. It could have just stuck up without running into anything). Except for this, assembly was not particularly difficult.

You use three AA batteries to power the sound. Once you hook up the spigot, you can put water in the sink and then pump it out through the spigot. The plastic food was recognizable as specific types of food, and the pots, plates, utensils, and bottles are distinct and fairly sturdy. Since it is merely pressure that fastens the joints together, this could come apart under especially hard play, but it's unlikely a two-year-old will cause any problems with it. Overall, I'm pleased and my niece is extremely happy to play with it when visiting my house.

UPDATE: The stickers are coming off after about a week, and not just because of use. They just didn't stick well to the water bottle and utensils. The handles on the cupboard about the oven is difficult to open because there's nothing to really get a grip on the handle. It's the perfect height for a 2-year-old, but my 4.5-year-old niece has to kneel to use it. (We wanted something small since we don't have lots of room to store the toys, but this maybe isn't something that will span a large age range.)

text_fidelity_a:
Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months + This frog is loud and a bit annoying, but it's still cute!

When this toy comes out of the box, you'll have to put together 3 different pieces. The head has to be attached to the body, and a little spring part attaches to the side. There are 6 different colored balls, too.

This toy does NOT come with batteries. You'll need 4 AA batteries, along with a small screwdriver(Phillips head or flat, either one) to get them into the toy.

There are 4 "piano" keys on the front that make sounds, and there's also the main button that will start the music playing and the mouth to bouncing. The inside of the mouth is soft. When the main button is pressed, the inside of the mouth will move around, and make the balls bounce. When the ball hits the center of the mouth, the bouncing will usually cause the ball to bounce outside of the mouth. This is fun for children to then go grabbing the stray balls. If the child is really young, you'll be the one grabbing the balls. (They will go rolling under couches and beds, so try to play it in an area that will result in minimal lost balls.)

Overall, this is a fun toy for young children/babies. The average mama of babies won't want it around too much, though. Between the noise and running after balls, it's a bit exhausting. For mamas of children that are old enough to chase after the balls, it's a great way to burn built up energy on a rainy day! (If playing on carpet, the balls most likely won't roll quite so much.)
text_fidelity_b: Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months +
